title: Behold the Savior of Mankind
description: Behold the Savior of Mankind in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Samuel Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 211.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold the Sa-vior of man-kind Nailed to the shame-ful tree! How vast the love that Him in-clined To bleed and die for thee!

lines: How vast the love that Him inclined
To bleed and die for thee!
Hark how He groans while nature shakes
The Temple’s veil in sunder breaks,
See where He bows His sacred head!
He bows His head and dies.
But soon He’ll break death’s envious chain
O Lamb of God, was ever pain,

licence: Public domain: Samuel Wesley died in 1735.
credits: Words by Samuel Wesley (1662–1735), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
